children: Prabhudas Lilladher's research report on Tata Power Company

Tata Power (TPWR) reported a strong Q2FY27 performance, with EBITDA growing 11% YoY and adjusted PAT rising 72% YoY. The PAT beat was primarily driven by (1) Coal SPV profitability improving to USD9/t versus ~USD6/t QoQ and USD2/t YoY, benefiting from higher imported coal prices, and (2) standalone PAT growth of 63% YoY, supported by Mundra operations and higher DSM revenues. Management reiterated its FY27 renewable capacity addition target of 2.5 GW, of which 25% was achieved in 1HFY27. Renewable commissioning is expected to accelerate as evacuation infrastructure improves. The company has also appointed Sanjay Banga, currently CEO & MD of Tata Power Renewable Energy, as CEO-designate of TPWR. Tata Power remains on track to achieve its FY27 capex guidance of INR250bn, having incurred INR100bn in 1HFY27. It continues to strengthen its storage portfolio, with the 1,000 MW Bhivpuri PSP targeted for H1CY29 and the newly approved 1,800 MW Shirota PSP targeted for CY31. On Mundra, the SPPA with Gujarat has been signed, while discussions with the remaining four states are progressing, with two at an advanced stage. Regarding the Kleros dispute, management remains confident of a favourable outcome. The Singapore Court of Appeal hearing is scheduled for 19 January 2027, with enforcement proceedings expected to take 3–6 months.

We retain ACCUMULATE with a TP of INR414, implying 11x 1HFY29E EV/EBITDA. The outcome of the Kleros dispute remains the key stock catalyst, given that Tata Power has not recognised any provision against the USD490mn claim (excluding interest). The balance sheet remains healthy with cash balances of INR111bn and net debt-to-equity of ~1.27x.
